deep.reconstruction:
Setting (base field S, implicit; the previous page is about reducing the group by adjoining a root of an auxiliary irreducible equation). Let f(x) = (x-r')(x-r'')...(x-r^(m)) be irreducible over S of degree m. Let phi(xi) = (xi-rho')...(xi-rho^(mu)) be irreducible over S of degree mu and normal: every root is a rational function of any one of them, so S(rho) is a Galois extension of S.

(1) Two factorizations. Over S(rho): f(x) = f_1(x,rho) f_2(x,rho) ... f_k(x,rho), with irreducible factors. Over S(r): phi(xi) = phi_1(xi,r) ... phi_k(xi,r). The two factorizations are matched: f_n(r,xi) is divisible by phi_n(xi,r), and phi_n(rho,x) is divisible by f_n(x,rho). This is the classical reciprocity of factorizations; both factorizations correspond to the irreducible factors of the bivariate norm. That they have the same number k of factors is asserted, not proved, on this page.

(2) Equal degrees of the phi_n. Because phi is normal, S(rho_i) = S(rho) for every root rho_i. Hence each factor phi_n over S(r) has degree [S(r,rho):S(r)] =: nu. So mu = k nu. Dedekind starts to name the roots of phi_1 as omega_j(r), crosses this out, and writes phi_1(xi,r) = Prod(xi - rho_1) = Prod(xi - omega_1(r)).

(3) Conjugation permutes the f_n. Let rho and rho' = theta(rho) be two roots of phi, where theta is the rational function expressing rho' in rho (an automorphism of S(rho)/S). Since f has coefficients in S, f(x) = Prod f_i(x,rho) = Prod f_i(x,theta rho). Claim: each f_i(x,theta rho) is again irreducible over S(rho). Proof: suppose f_1(x,theta rho) = f_1'(x,rho) f_1''(x,rho). Put rho = theta^{-1}(rho'). Then f_1(x,rho') = f_1'(x,theta^{-1}rho') f_1''(x,theta^{-1}rho') is a nontrivial factorization over S(rho') = S(rho). This contradicts the irreducibility of f_1(x,rho') over S(rho'), which follows by conjugating the hypothesis (implicit). Hence f_i(x,theta rho) = f_j(x,rho) for some j: every substitution rho -> rho' induces a definite permutation of the factors f_1, ..., f_k.

(4) Degree count via the norm. Let m_1 = deg f_1. Then Prod_{rho_i} f_1(x,rho_i) is the norm N_{S(rho)/S}(f_1). It is a power of the irreducible f, of degree m_1 mu, so it equals f(x)^{m_1 mu / m}. Let delta = gcd(m, mu); the manuscript says 'der groesste Divisor von m', surely meaning the gcd of m and mu. Since m divides m_1 mu, one gets m_1 = delta_1 m/delta, and analogously mu_1 = delta_1 mu/delta. Together with m = k m_1 (equal degrees of the f_i, from (3)) and mu = k mu_1 (with mu_1 = nu), this gives delta = k delta_1. Thus k divides gcd(m, mu), with m = kn, n = m_1, mu = k nu.

Filled check (mine): the degree [S(r,rho):S] equals m nu = mu n. With mu = k nu this forces m = kn, consistent with the page.

(5) Beginning of the composition law. The substitution rho -> rho' sends f_u to f_u', i.e. f_u'(x,rho) = f_u(x,rho'). The substitution rho' -> rho'' sends f_u' to f_u'', i.e. f_u''(x,rho') = f_u'(x,rho''). In theta-notation, f_u'(x,rho) = f_u(x,theta rho). Substituting rho -> theta_1 rho (or theta rho) gives f_u'(x, theta rho) = f_u(x, theta theta_1 rho). The page breaks off at f_u''(x,theta rho) = f_u'(x, ...).

Purpose: to show that the map from the group of phi (i.e. of S(rho)/S) to permutations of the factors is a homomorphism. Adjoining rho reduces the group G of f to a subgroup T, invariant under conjugation. The next page proves, for T with theta T = T theta, that the cosets T, T theta, ..., T theta^(n-1) partition G and n divides p. This is Galois's theorem on adjoining a root of a normal auxiliary equation, worked out in the style of Dedekind's 1856-58 Goettingen Galois lectures.
errors: 'delta der groesste Divisor von m' must mean the greatest common divisor of m and mu; as written it is meaningless (the largest divisor of m is m).
The equality of the numbers of factors (k for both f over S(rho) and phi over S(r)) and the exact correspondence f_n <-> phi_n are asserted without proof on this page (true; standard).

In the composition line, f_u'(x,theta rho) = f_u(x, theta theta_1 rho) has inconsistent indices. From f_u'(x,rho) = f_u(x,theta rho), substituting rho -> theta_1 rho gives f_u'(x,theta_1 rho) = f_u(x, theta(theta_1 rho)). Either the left side should carry theta_1, or the right side should be theta theta rho. This is a minor slip in an unfinished line.

The relation m = k m_1 (all f_i of equal degree) is used in the degree bookkeeping; it follows from step (3) (the factors are permuted transitively by conjugation), but transitivity is not explicitly stated.
Irreducibility of f_1(x,rho') over S(rho') is used as hypothesis ('contra hyp.'); it follows by conjugating rho -> rho'. Fine but implicit.

results.what: Over S(rho), rho a root of a normal irreducible equation phi, an irreducible f splits into k conjugate irreducible factors of equal degree, permuted by the substitutions rho -> theta(rho); correspondingly phi splits over S(r) into k factors of equal degree nu, with mu = k nu, m = k n.
results.modern_name: Splitting of an irreducible polynomial over a Galois extension (conjugate factors of equal degree; natural irrationalities)
results.usually_credited_to: Galois (Memoire 1831, Prop. II/III); systematized by Jordan (1870); Dedekind's version in his 1856-58 Goettingen lectures

results.what: Reciprocity: the factorization of f over S(rho) and of phi over S(r) correspond factor by factor (f_n(r,xi) divisible by phi_n(xi,r), etc.)
results.modern_name: Reciprocity of factorizations / factorization of the compositum S(r) tensor S(rho)

results.what: Norm of the factor: Prod over conjugates of f_1(x,rho_i) = f(x)^(m_1 mu/m), whence k divides gcd(m, mu).
results.modern_name: Norm of an irreducible factor is a power of the irreducible polynomial; number of factors divides gcd of degrees

results.what: Substitutions of rho induce permutations of the factors, with a composition rule (toward a homomorphism to the group of factor permutations; quotient by a normal subgroup on the next page).
results.modern_name: Action of Gal(S(rho)/S) on the factors; quotient group G/T
results.usually_credited_to: Galois; Dedekind's lectures (first explicit quotient-group treatment)

deep.surprise_reason: This is standard Galois-theoretic material (Galois's proposition on adjoining a root of a normal auxiliary equation). Dedekind's working through it in the 1850s Galois lectures is documented (Purkert 1976, Scharlau 1981 edition of his Galois lectures). This page is a draft of known content.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import symbols, sqrt, factor_list; x=symbols('x'); factor_list(x**4-2, extension=sqrt(2))
checkable.asserts: Over Q(sqrt2) (phi = xi**2-2, normal, mu=2), f = x**4-2 (m=4) splits into k=2 factors of equal degree n=2 (x**2-sqrt2)(x**2+sqrt2), so m = k n and k | gcd(4,2).

checkable.sympy: from sympy import symbols, sqrt, expand; x=symbols('x'); expand((x**2-sqrt(2))*(x**2+sqrt(2))) - (x**4-2)
checkable.asserts: Norm identity: product of f_1(x,rho) over the conjugates rho=+-sqrt2 equals f(x)**(m_1*mu/m) = f**(2*2/4) = f (difference is 0).

checkable.sympy: from sympy import symbols, root, factor_list; X=symbols('X'); factor_list(X**2-2, extension=root(2,4))
checkable.asserts: Reciprocal factorization: phi = xi**2-2 over Q(r), r=2**(1/4), splits into k=2 linear factors (nu=1), mu = k nu = 2.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import symbols, sqrt, I, factor_list; x=symbols('x'); factor_list(x**3-2, extension=sqrt(3)*I)
checkable.asserts: f = x**3-2 (m=3) stays irreducible over Q(sqrt(-3)) (root field of the normal phi = xi**2+xi+1, mu=2): k=1, consistent with k | gcd(3,2)=1.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import symbols, sqrt, factor_list; x=symbols('x'); factor_list(x**4+1, extension=sqrt(2))
checkable.asserts: x**4+1 splits over Q(sqrt2) into the two conjugate quadratics x**2 +- sqrt2*x + 1, which are interchanged by sqrt2 -> -sqrt2 (substitution of rho permutes the factors).
